title: Axial Hub Transit — Reimagine Console IA & Workspace Switching
creator: Ava Chen
description: Redesign the Console information architecture and workspace switching flow to reduce cognitive load for multi-tenant users and improve discoverability of rollouts, cost lenses, and per-model dashboards. The goal is a single, axial hub that surfaces the currently active workspace, a lightweight contextual rail for quick-task actions (rollout controls, canary toggles, cost breakdown quickcards), and a progressive disclosure pattern for deep dashboard surfaces. This ticket covers the design exploration, prototype handoff, and early usability feedback cycles needed before ENG can implement a canary UI behind a feature flag.
context: Current sidebar is overloaded — users report 3x time to find rollout controls during incident drills
Multiple workspace switch patterns exist (modal, header menu, left-rail dropdown) causing state inconsistency in analytics
Cost visibility lives in several places (route cards, model pages, billing) which makes quick triage difficult for platform teams
review_feedback: Liam Patel (PM): prefer preserving current keyboard shortcuts for workspace switcher; propose adding a persistent shortcut hint in the axial hub
Sofia Martinez (Eng): backend should expose active-workspace context in the session token; blocking until ENG-43022 exposes the endpoint
Ethan Brooks (Security): audit log requirement for switcher actions accepted; will require an opt-in flag for Private customers
decisions: Adopt an 'axial hub' concept: compact left rail with expandable hub panel that anchors workspace level controls and quickcards
Move costly/rare controls (project settings, billing) into a secondary drawer to declutter immediate navigation
Session persistence: switching workspaces updates URL + session cookie for cross-tab continuity
Rollouts control will surface as a contextual card in the hub with a lightweight canary toggle and link to full rollout page
tradeoffs: Compact hub reduces visual clutter but consumes vertical space when expanded on small viewports — temporary compromise: collapse into badge-only mode on < 1000px widths
Keeping shortcuts increases discoverability for power users but risks confusion for new users — include an onboarding tooltip and an accessible keyboard hint
Surface-level cost quickcards provide rapid triage at the expense of duplicating some metric views found in dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Prototype validated with 6 internal users across Platform, Growth, and SRE teams with <= 2 failed tasks for workspace switch
Design tokens and component specs exported to Figma library and referenced in GH PR
Edge-case flows documented: multi-tab switch, guest access, workspace permissions preventing switch
Accessibility: AXE baseline run passes with no high violations for hub components
